steps.description: Fit the differential expression model on the raw integer counts from counts.csv. Import the count matrix directly into DESeqDataSetFromMatrix — the counts are gene-level integers from STAR + featureCounts, so apply no gene-length correction and do not route them through tximport. Set the reference level of the condition factor explicitly to the control level named in metadata.csv (do not rely on alphabetical ordering) and name the contrast as the triple (condition, treated, control) so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Pre-filter minimally: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size). Let DESeq2 estimate median-of-ratios size factors inside the model; do not pre-normalize. Run the Wald test, keep the default count-outlier policy (with 3 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance outliers and sets their p-values to NA — report how many genes are NA from this cause separately from those the independent filter removed). Shrink the reported log2 fold change with apeglm on the treated-vs-control coefficient, keeping the unshrunken estimate and its standard error alongside. Call results() with alpha = 0.05, independent filtering on, BH adjustment. Also draw the GC-content and gene-length bias diagnostic required for aligner+counter counts: plot the log ratio of each sample's counts against the median sample versus gene GC content and versus gene length, using a human gene annotation resolved from the environment's reference store; cqn and EDASeq are not installed here, so if a trend is present, report it as an uncorrected limitation and state that correction would require cqn or a bias-aware re-quantification — do not attempt an ad hoc correction. If no human gene-length/GC annotation can be resolved, state that the diagnostic could not be drawn and continue; this affects an annotation, not the DE result. As the permitted robustness second method, run the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts, same filter policy and same design, at the same alpha. Write the DESeq2 results table (baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue, padj) for all tested genes, the edgeR table, and the two significant gene sets.

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE (DESeq2 + edgeR)
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12,000 x 6 raw integer gene-level count matrix (counts.csv) produced by STAR alignment and featureCounts, with a 6 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv) giving one condition label per sample: 3 drug-treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch. Because the counts are integer gene counts from an aligner and a counter, they go straight into a negative-binomial count model with no length correction and no tximport (R-0064) — this is the specific point the research question raises. The plan runs three steps. T1S1 does sample structure QC on the 6 samples: library sizes, blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-to-sample distance heatmap, so any sample that does not group with its condition is seen before any test is fitted; with n=3 per group there is no batch variable to colour by, so condition is the only annotation. T1S2 fits the DESeq2 model on the raw counts with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, an explicitly set reference level (control) and the contrast named as condition/treated/control, then the Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change, independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment at alpha 0.05. Because the counts carry no quantifier-side bias model, the same step draws the GC-content and gene-length bias diagnostic (log count ratio of each sample against the median sample); cqn and EDASeq are absent from this environment, so if a trend appears the step reports it as an uncorrected limitation rather than silently proceeding. The edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test runs on the same counts and design as the permitted second method for a robustness check. T1S3 assembles the report: MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, the gene table carrying both unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold changes with the standard error, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the high-confidence set, and an explicit statement of the power limit — with 3 replicates per group only a minority of true effects, mostly large fold changes, are detectable, so absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change. No enrichment step is planned: the research question asks which genes are differentially expressed and nothing more.

flags.message: With counts from an aligner and a counter, no bias model runs at the quantification, thus a sample-specific effect of the GC content and of the gene length can remain in the counts, and such an effect adds a difference between samples that the between-sample normalization does not remove. Draw the diagnostic: for each pair of samples, or for each sample against the median sample, plot the log ratio of the counts against the GC content of the genes and against the gene length, and report a trend. For a 3' tag library, the count does not depend on the gene length, thus plot the GC content only. Conditional quantile normalization (cqn) and the GC-content normalization of EDASeq are the tools of record for the correction, and both are absent from this pool. If the diagnostic shows a trend, state it in the plan and ask for cqn, or for a new quantification with a bias-aware quantifier such as Salmon with its GC bias model. If the diagnostic shows no trend, state the check and continue.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.
